basic_profile.headline: Chief Security Officer | Ex-Superintendent of Police | Expert in Risk, Fraud Prevention & Supply Chain Security | Board-Certified Director
basic_profile.name: Firoze Zia Hussain
basic_profile.summary:
I am a forward-thinking security and risk management leader with 30+ years of experience spanning law enforcement, corporate security, logistics, and technology-led risk prevention. Currently serving as Chief Security Officer at Delhivery, I design and oversee security, trust, and safety frameworks across India’s largest logistics network — covering 24 automated sort centers, 90+ fulfilment hubs, 2,500+ delivery centers, and 58,000+ employees.

Previously, as a Superintendent of Police in Pondicherry, I specialized in trafficking, narcotics enforcement, cybercrime, and community policing, achieving a 99% conviction rate and pioneering India’s early cybercrime investigations.

I’ve driven business continuity, fraud prevention, safety, and compliance strategies for Fortune 500s, airports, defense, banking, and e-commerce. My leadership philosophy is built on change management, operational excellence, and digital transformation — blending public service discipline with corporate agility.

Recognized with awards including the Golden Peacock Award, SECONA Shield for Security Project of the Year, and Assocham SME Excellence Award, I also hold patents and publications on e-governance, fraud detection, and women’s safety tech solutions.

Specialties: Corporate Security, Supply Chain Risk, Fraud Analytics, Business Continuity, Regulatory Compliance, Project Management, Independent Directorship

past.company_description: he Government of India, officially known as the Union Government, and also known as the Central Government, was established by the Constitution of India, and is the governing authority of a union of 28 states and seven union territories, collectively called the Republic of India. It is seated in New Delhi, the capital of India.The government comprises three branches: the executive, the legislative and the judiciary. The executive branch headed by the President, who is the Head of State and exercises his or her power directly or through officers subordinate to him.[1] The Legislative branch or the Parliament consists of the lower house, the Lok Sabha, and the upper house, the Rajya Sabha, as well as the president. The Judicial branch has the Supreme Court at its apex, 21 High Courts, and numerous civil, criminal and family courts at the district level.The basic civil and criminal laws governing the citizens of India are set down in major parliamentary legislation, such as the Civil Procedure Code, the Indian Penal Code, and the Criminal Procedure Code. The union and individual state governments consist of executive, legislative and judicial branches. The legal system as applicable to the federal and individual state governments is based on the English Common and Statutory Law. India accepts International Court of Justice jurisdiction with several reservations.
